feature_config.why_lfcc: LFCC is the official ASVspoof 2019/2021 baseline front-end; linear filter spacing keeps high-frequency resolution where vocoder/TTS artifacts live, which mel spacing compresses away.

verdict_before.text: Timing alone separates the classes well (lead_silence_s EER 0.1799), so this data carries the known ASVspoof silence-duration shortcut.

verdict_after.text: Timing alone is weakly predictive (total_s EER 0.3999) -- some leakage, but far from a free solution.

silence_leakage.note: Every model input is a fixed-length window, so absolute clip duration cannot reach the model regardless; these probes measure what the raw data leaks, and the trimmed-vs-untrimmed models below measure whether the model actually exploited it.
silence_leakage.duration_vs_content_note: HYPOTHESIS, not a finding (tested by Phase 2B's silence ablations): the duration probes top out at EER 0.1799, but the model trained on untrimmed audio reaches 0.0097. One explanation is that the silence's content (e.g. noise floor / room tone in bonafide recordings vs. near-digital silence in synthesised clips) matters beyond its length -- but the gap alone doesn't prove it, since the model also sees speech position and silence/speech interaction, which a single timing number can't capture.

cross_dataset_spot_check.note: Cross-dataset spot-check skipped; in-domain results above are unaffected.
cross_dataset_spot_check.root_cause: In-the-Wild ships as a zip, so `datasets` hands back a chained fsspec URL (zip://...::hf://...) rather than raw bytes, and libsndfile cannot open that path directly. Fixed in engines/voice/data.py (open via fsspec and hand soundfile the bytes); needs a re-run to produce a number.

closing_paragraph: Headline: an LCNN on LFCC features reaches 0.2380 EER on a held-out, speaker-disjoint test split of 1825 clips drawn from a 6000-clip subset of the ASVspoof 2019 LA evaluation partition. Silence leakage: before trimming, the most predictive timing measure alone reached EER 0.1799 (lead_silence_s); after trimming, 0.3999. Timing alone separates the classes well (lead_silence_s EER 0.1799), so this data carries the known ASVspoof silence-duration shortcut. Training on untrimmed features scored 0.2282 EER *better* (0.0097), i.e. the model does exploit silence when it is left in -- trimming removes a real shortcut rather than a hypothetical one. Speaker leakage did not inflate the number here: random-split EER (0.2371) is not better than the speaker-disjoint EER (0.2380). Out of domain: the spot-check did not run, so nothing is claimed about generalization. Scope limit: every clip comes from the LA evaluation partition, so the same spoofing systems appear in train and test. Performance against unseen attack types is not measured.

interpretation_added_after_the_run.corrections: 2026-09-28: notes corrected per Phase 2B pre-flight -- removed the false claim that 0.0097 beat the 2019 challenge winner (~0.2% EER on the official protocol; not comparable anyway), relabelled the silence-content explanation as a hypothesis, and replaced 'speaker leakage is nothing' with 'not detectable at this sample size'. The measured numbers above are unchanged.
notes: The 0.0097 EER untrimmed model is the number a careless pipeline would have reported. It is far better than the official LFCC-GMM baseline range, which for a small CNN is itself the sign of a shortcut. (No published-number comparison is valid: those are on the official protocol, this is not.)

HYPOTHESIS (tested by Phase 2B's silence ablations): the best timing-only probe reaches EER 0.1799 while the model given the actual silent samples reaches 0.0097, which suggests silence content matters beyond its length -- not yet shown.

Speaker leakage measured at -0.0009 EER: not detectable at this sample size (the strongest claim allowed with ~180 bonafide test clips and one seed). Unlike the graph engine's temporal-vs-random gap of +0.26, sharing speakers across the split did not inflate this task. Plausible reason: spoof detection keys on synthesis artifacts, not voice identity. Caveat: single seed, and the two splits have different test sets (1825 vs 1800 clips), so a difference this small is inside the noise either way.

Not comparable to published ASVspoof numbers: the official protocol trains on attacks A01-A06 and tests on unseen A07-A19, while this setup trains and tests on the same attack family, and uses 3282 training clips rather than the full 25380-clip train partition.

The trimmed model is data-limited: only 353 bonafide clips in training, best validation EER at epoch 3 while training loss kept falling to 0.166 -- it overfits quickly. A larger N_CLIPS is the obvious next lever.
